statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. All 24 published hours fall inside the scheduled weekend halt of CME equity-index futures and the NAS100 CFD, so no pathological Nasdaq-100 price path can form inside the window, while the rate, energy and diplomatic backdrop behind moderate Stress remains unresolved.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold for every published hour because no tradable Nasdaq-100 venue exists before the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, roughly nineteen hours beyond the final slot. Stress describes a 5.18% 10-year yield, $92.41 WTI and an unanswered Iranian Hormuz proposal rather than any observed mean-reversion failure. Reopen gap risk falls outside this window.
headline: Nasdaq-100 stays inside the scheduled CME weekend closure after an orderly Friday advance; Tail at its floor while a post-crisis 10-year yield, $92 crude and unanswered Hormuz diplomacy keep Stress in the mid-40s
body: Friday's session closed in orderly, two-sided fashion and no Nasdaq-100 venue has traded since. Cash NDX finished 30,608.14, up 129.28 points or 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and about 0.19% below the session high, against a 30,478.86 previous close. NQ December 2026 futures last printed 30,889.25, up 122.50 or 0.40%, within a 30,679.00-30,997.25 range. VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 in a 14.68-15.94 range from a 15.67 previous close, verified on Yahoo Finance's ^VIX quote page. All three major US averages posted weekly gains: the Dow rose 0.93% to 51,828.62, snapping a three-week losing streak, the S&P 500 rose 0.51% to 7,743.41 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.48% to 27,068.72. Retracements occurred repeatedly through the session and the index did not hold an extreme into the close, so none of the mean-reversion-failure amplifiers this contract requires were present when the tape stopped. CME equity-index futures settled at 21:00Z on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, roughly nineteen hours past the final published hour, so every slot in this assessment sits inside a scheduled closure with no tradable venue. That is why Tail is held near its floor rather than inferred from Friday's mildly positive tone. The environment behind Stress is genuinely unresolved. The Federal Reserve's H.15 release for September 24 shows the 10-year Treasury constant maturity at 5.18%, its highest level since the global financial crisis, with the 2-year at 4.87% and the effective federal funds rate at 3.88%. The FOMC statement of September 16 raised the target range by a quarter point to 3.75-4.00%, and the Fed's own calendar puts the next decision at October 27-28, which markets still treat as live. WTI stands at $92.41, down 2.33%, with Brent at $104.32, after Iran's foreign minister proposed at the UN General Assembly to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days in exchange for lifting the US naval blockade, waiving sanctions on Iranian oil sales and observing a ceasefire. Fresh weekend reporting dated September 26 adds that Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says Hormuz security cannot be restored through military action and that the choice now rests with Washington, while a State Department spokesperson said diplomatic channels remain open. Washington has not accepted the terms, the strait has not reopened, no ceasefire has begun and US Central Command has redirected 122 commercial vessels to enforce the blockade, so the closure and its supply premium remain in place. Friday's leadership was dispersed rather than one-way, with Microsoft closing at its highest level of the year while Meta fell 3.3% even after a roughly 13% weekly gain following its Muse AI agent launch, which argues against aligned breadth as a Tail amplifier. The coming week carries Dallas Fed manufacturing on Monday, JOLTS and consumer confidence on Tuesday, ADP with August PCE and final Q2 GDP on Wednesday, ISM Manufacturing on Thursday and September payrolls with the unemployment rate on Friday; Micron reports fiscal Q4 after the close on September 30. Those are forward checkpoints that raise Stress and shape Confidence; under this contract they do not by themselves raise Tail before a price path is observed. Shared Finviz context was read at the start of this run. It is dated 02:04Z, which places it outside the 90-minute freshness window, and it reports collectionStatus partial with both its futures and calendar sections unavailable. Its latest-session breadth, megacap and semiconductor readings were therefore treated as stale, explicitly non-real-time context and used only as weak corroboration of Friday's dispersed leadership and firm semiconductor tone, with its headlines used for discovery only. Every level quoted above comes from a primary source verified directly during this run.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 published hours the Claude state ranged between Tail 8 and 22 and never approached the block threshold. The opening stretch from 04:00Z to 05:00Z on September 25 held Tail at 18 in normal conditions. The European and US cash stretch from 06:00Z to 14:00Z produced four trend-up prints and a run of WATCH states at Tail 20-22 as the index worked higher, and the 13:00Z slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable rather than reconstructed. From 15:00Z conditions settled back to mixed at Tail 18-19, and the final seven hours fell to Tail 12, 10, 10, 9, 9, 8 and 8 as CME futures settled into the weekend closure and no tradable price path remained. Stress ranged between 45 and 58, holding in the mid-50s through the cash session before easing steadily to 45 by the last published hour, and Confidence held between 83 and 88 throughout.
outlookSummary: The entire published window falls inside the scheduled CME weekend closure: futures settled at 21:00Z on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, roughly nineteen hours past the final slot. Tail is held between 7 and 9 for all 24 hours because sustained mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path, and none of the inherited amplifiers, shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension, or an index pinned near an extreme, can be observed while every Nasdaq-100 venue is shut. Stress eases from 44 to 41 through the deepest part of the closure and firms back to 46 by the final hours as the reopen and a week carrying PCE, final Q2 GDP, ISM Manufacturing and September payrolls approach. Confidence decays from 82 to 65 across the window because later hours sit progressively further from the verified Friday evidence set, while the exchange calendar anchoring the low Tail stays certain. Weekend geopolitical developments, above all a US response to Iran's Hormuz terms, would transmit only as headlines within this window; their earliest possible price expression is the Sunday reopen, which lies outside it.
